novel_features.name: Bulk Attachment Export
novel_features.description: Download every attachment matching a Gmail search query to a local directory — invoice extraction in one command.
novel_features.rationale: Requires resolving attachment IDs across multiple messages from local SQLite, then batching gmail.users.messages.attachments.get calls — 60+ lines of Python in a single command.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you need to bulk-extract invoice PDFs, report attachments, or any attachment type from a set of emails — without writing a script.

novel_features.name: Sender Leaderboard
novel_features.description: Rank your top email senders by volume with unsubscribe link detection — the inbox transparency view Gmail's UI never shows you.
novel_features.rationale: SQL GROUP BY from_address across synced messages with List-Unsubscribe join — no single Gmail API endpoint returns per-sender aggregates.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when you need to find who floods your inbox before a cleanup session, or identify newsletter candidates for bulk unsubscribe.

novel_features.name: Newsletter List
novel_features.description: Surface every sender with a List-Unsubscribe header grouped by domain — your actionable unsubscribe queue.
novel_features.rationale: Queries local SQLite for messages where list_unsubscribe is populated (parsed at sync time from RFC 2369 headers) — impossible via a single Gmail API call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before a Friday inbox cleanup to get a ranked list of newsletters with direct unsubscribe URLs — no web UI clicking required.

novel_features.name: Inbox Digest
novel_features.description: Your daily inbox summary in one command — threads grouped by label with sender, subject, and unread count.
novel_features.rationale: Joins threads + messages + message_labels in local SQLite; groups by label; no live API call needed after sync — what the Gmail mobile digest notification should be.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use every morning to get a structured inbox summary pipeable to an agent or shell script without opening Gmail.

novel_features.name: Attachment Inventory
novel_features.description: List all attachments in your synced mailbox filtered by MIME type or Gmail query — zero API calls after sync.
novel_features.rationale: Queries local attachments table joined with messages; Gmail MIME structure requires multi-step API fetches making a local index uniquely fast.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before running attachments export to preview what will be downloaded, or to find a specific file without opening Gmail.

novel_features.name: Sync Status
novel_features.description: Check when your local mailbox was last synced and whether the history token is still fresh.
novel_features.rationale: Reads local sync_state table — last timestamp, history token age, total synced count — making silent token expiry visible before running queries.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before running any local-store query to verify your data is current and diagnose why results might be stale.

novel_features.name: Unread Age Histogram
novel_features.description: See how old your unread mail is — bucketed by today / 1-7d / 8-30d / 30-90d / 90d+ per label.
novel_features.rationale: SQL GROUP BY date_bucket on unread messages in local SQLite — no live API call can return this aggregate across a large mailbox.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use during inbox cleanup to understand the shape of your unread pile before deciding what to bulk-archive.

novel_features.name: Outbound Volume by Domain
novel_features.description: Count outbound emails to a recipient domain in a time window — the one-command compliance audit.
novel_features.rationale: Queries synced SENT messages by To-header domain in local SQLite — no Gmail API endpoint returns sent-volume-by-recipient-domain.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use before a compliance review to verify email volume to a customer or partner without exporting all mail.

narrative.headline: Your entire Gmail mailbox in a local SQLite database — searchable offline, queryable with SQL, and pipeline-ready for agents.
narrative.value_prop: Every Gmail MCP tool makes live API calls for every operation. The Gmail CLI syncs your mailbox once and lets you query it as a database: FTS search in milliseconds, sender analytics, newsletter detection, attachment pipelines, inbox digests — all offline. Plus the full live API surface for sending, labeling, threading, and managing settings.
narrative.auth_narrative: Gmail uses OAuth2. Run `gmail-pp-cli auth login` to open a browser window for the Google OAuth2 consent screen. Your refresh token is stored in `~/.config/gmail-pp-cli/token.json` and refreshed automatically. Set `GMAIL_CLIENT_ID` and `GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET` from a Google Cloud Console project with the Gmail API enabled.

quickstart.comment: Authenticate via browser — stores refresh token locally
Pull all messages, threads, labels, and attachment metadata into local SQLite
Morning inbox summary — no API call needed after sync
Sender leaderboard with newsletter detection — Friday cleanup starting point
Bulk-download all matching attachments to a local directory

troubleshoots.fix: Run `gmail-pp-cli auth login` — token is missing or expired. Delete `~/.config/gmail-pp-cli/token.json` and re-authenticate if refresh fails.

troubleshoots.symptom: stale command shows history token expired
troubleshoots.fix: Run `gmail-pp-cli sync --full` to re-sync from scratch. History tokens expire after ~7 days of no incremental sync.

troubleshoots.symptom: digest / senders / attachments return no results
troubleshoots.fix: Run `gmail-pp-cli sync --full` first — these commands query the local store, not the live API.
The sync respects Gmail's rate limits with exponential backoff. Large mailboxes (100k+ messages) may take 60+ minutes on first sync. The sync is resumable — rerun if interrupted.

narrative.when_to_use: Use the Gmail CLI when you need to work with email data at scale: bulk attachment extraction, sender analytics, inbox triage automation, or building pipelines that process email content. Ideal for developers and power users who want offline access to their mailbox, SQL-queryable email data, and agent-friendly JSON output for downstream automation.
